s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with radiation to the jaw and diaphoresis
salient_findings: Chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
key_facts: Subjective fevers, rhinorrhea, dry cough, and sinus congestion 4 days prior to presentation
3 hours of substernal pressure that resolved spontaneously the day prior to presentation
Constant chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein
Initial serum troponin I level of 6.18 ng/mL
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with radiation to the jaw and diaphoresis
salient_findings: Chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
key_facts: Subjective fevers, rhinorrhea, dry cough, and sinus congestion 4 days prior to presentation
3 hours of substernal pressure that resolved spontaneously the day prior to presentation
Constant chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein
Initial serum troponin I level of 6.18 ng/mL
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with chest pressure, elevated inflammatory markers (erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein), and normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography, along with the ECG findings of ST-segment elevations and PR-segment depression, are consistent with pericarditis. The absence of significant left ventricular dysfunction or coronary artery disease also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: myocardial infarction
rejected.why: Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography and lack of significant left ventricular dysfunction make this less likely

rejected.label: acute coronary syndrome
rejected.why: Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography and normal cardiac examination make this less likely

rejected.label: takotsubo cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: Lack of significant left ventricular dysfunction and normal transthoracic echocardiogram results make this less likely

rejected.label: heart failure
rejected.why: Normal left ventricular end-diastolic pressure and normal transthoracic echocardiogram results make this less likely
